title-slide.en: Welcome to session twelve: Solver and sensitivity.
Today we solve CellCo's product mix in Excel Solver, and learn to answer what-if questions from the sensitivity report.

route.en: First the simplex method and Solver, then the sensitivity report. After the break, allowable ranges, the what-if hotline, and the start of workshop five.

simplex.en: The simplex method starts at a corner and moves along an edge to a better neighbor, until no neighbor is better.
From the origin, P has the larger margin, so simplex increases P until power-cell demand stops it at sixty.
At that corner, increasing E still pays, until coating stops it at thirty.
At thirty and sixty, no edge improves the contribution. The method stops after two steps.

solver.en: In Excel, put the decisions, the margins, and the hours used and available in separate cells.
The objective cell is a sum product of margins and decisions, and each constraint row compares hours used with hours available.
In the Solver dialog, choose the Simplex method, make variables non-negative, and ask for the sensitivity report.
Keep data, formulas and decisions separate. A model with numbers typed inside formulas cannot be audited or re-run with new data.

report.en: This is the sensitivity report for the product mix.
The upper table covers the decision variables: their final values, reduced costs, and the allowable changes in their margins.
The lower table covers the constraints: their final values, shadow prices, and the allowable changes in their right-hand sides.
The shadow prices, fifteen, zero and three, are exactly the dual solution from session eleven.

reading.en: A shadow price is the change in the optimal objective per unit increase in a right-hand side, holding all other data fixed.
The allowable increase and decrease give the range over which that price stays valid. For coating, from 180 to 300 hours.
A reduced cost tells how much a margin must improve before a product enters the plan. It is zero for products already made.
Inside a range, the same constraints stay binding, so the answer moves in a straight line. At the edge, a new constraint binds and the price changes.

break.en: Let us take a ten-minute break.
Afterwards: what happens to the coating shadow price beyond three hundred hours?

price-explorer.en: This chart re-solves the model for every level of the chosen resource and plots the optimal contribution.
Each straight piece is one allowable range, and its slope is the shadow price.
For coating, the slope is fifteen between 180 and 300 hours, then drops to zero once formation binds.
Switch to formation hours. The curve is flat at today's level, because formation has idle hours.

act1.en: Activity, the what-if hotline. Work in groups of four for twenty-five minutes.
I will play the plant manager and call with five questions: coating overtime, renting out coating hours, a formation failure, more power-cell orders, and a lower margin for energy-storage cells.
Answer each question from the sensitivity report alone, and name the line you used. Then re-solve to check.

act1-answer.en: Overtime at ten thousand yuan per hour is worth buying, up to sixty hours, for a gain of 300 thousand a week.
The minimum rent for a coating hour is fifteen thousand yuan. Losing thirty formation hours changes nothing, because 45 are idle.
Ten more megawatt hours of power-cell orders add thirty thousand. And a margin of 25 for energy-storage cells keeps the plan, but lowers contribution by 150 thousand.
Remember that a shadow price answers one change at a time. For several changes together, re-solve.

w5.en: Workshop five starts now, for twenty minutes, and you finish it tonight.
Build the product-mix model in Solver, produce the sensitivity report, write the dual, and answer five pricing questions.
Quiz three, on today's material, is this evening.

debrief.en: Simplex walks from corner to better corner, and Solver's sensitivity report comes free with the solution.
A shadow price holds only inside its range: fifteen thousand yuan per coating hour from 180 to 300 hours, then zero.
Most what-if questions are answered by one report line, if the change is single and inside the range.
In session thirteen, we build transportation, blending and multi-period models, and add integer decisions.

exit.en: For the exit ticket: why is the coating shadow price zero above three hundred hours? Answer in one sentence.
